messages:
miguel: heads-up — i'm prototyping an "operator shim" that will sit in front of the dedicated-pool autoscaler. goal: separate cluster-level operator concerns (node lifecycle, taints) from quota/tenant signals so the autoscaler only sees a normalized interface.
anya: sounds good. curious what the normalized signals look like — do you mean something like desired_replicas + soft_headroom? :thinking:
miguel: exactly. thinking minimal contract: {desired_replicas, available_gpu_units, tenant_backlog_estimate, prewarm_slots_reserved}. keep it agnostic to how we count units (gpus vs fractional vram).
sam: i like that. i'd add an explicit "confidence" field for each signal so we can prefer conservative decisions when operator reports low confidence. e.g., confidence: low|medium|high. avoids oscillation during noisy telemetry.
miguel: good call. also planning an HTTP endpoint the scaler polls and a k8s CRD for desired state (for human/debug). example: ```GET /operator/v1/pool-signals
200 {
  "desired_replicas": 12,
  "available_gpu_units": 11.5,
  "backlog": 42,
  "prewarm_reserved": 2,
  "signals_confidence": "medium"
}
```
anya: how do we avoid double-counting if the autoscaler itself can request prewarm slots? we had issues where controller and tenant reservation tried to both prewarm and overshot quota.
miguel: plan is to make prewarm_reserved a unilateral declaration from the operator (it coordinates with node lifecycle). autoscaler can request a delta via the CRD but operator enforces caps from tenant quota and returns adjusted desired_replicas. autoscaler should treat operator response as authoritative.
sam: so operator enforces quotas -> autoscaler must surface rejections in metrics and not retry in tight loop. we should add a rejection_reason field to the response.
ken: +1 for rejection_reason. also we need to think about signal latency. operator uses kube events + cloud metrics and can be noisy for ~30s. autoscaler poll interval should be >= 15s and backoff on low confidence. otherwise we'll thrash.
sara: on the telemetry side — can we push these signals into the console dashboards? want to be able to quickly see operator vs autoscaler view. minimal labels: pool, region, tenant_id.
miguel: yes — operator will emit a prometheus metric per-pool (operator_pool_signals{pool="p1", region="us-west"} gauge) with breakdowns. also push an event when operator adjusts desired_replicas due to quota.
deploy-bot: deploy-ci: operator-shim branch merged to staging. smoke tests: scale up/down, quota-capped, and confidence-flap.
manuel: (reacting) :thumbsup:  // note: manuel lurks in infra but not in participants list — ignore
anya: edge case: cross-tenant sharing in a mixed instance type pool. operator needs to expose per-tenant effective unit conversion (e.g., 1 A100 = 1 unit, 1 T4 = 0.25). otherwise autoscaler can't reconcile.
miguel: i've added an optional "unit_conversion_map" blob: {"a100": 1.0, "t4": 0.25}. autoscaler can use it if it wants stable math, but operator will always return used units in the same canonical units.
sam: sounds solid. next step: write a short RFC describing the operator contract, the HTTP/CRD schema, and a couple of failure-mode tests. i'll take on the autoscaler-side changes once RFC is up.
anya: let's also include a small example of how the rollout works: operator reports desired_replicas=10 but quota caps to 8 -> autoscaler should scale to 8 and emit metric operator_quota_capped{pool="p1"}=1. put a runbook note: when capped for >5m, page infra-team.
miguel: noted. i'll draft the RFC today and add the metrics + CRD YAML to the repo. thanks all.
sam: thanks — ping when RFC is in PR and i'll review.
deploy-bot: ci/status: all tests passed on staging for operator-shim branch (build 472).
anya: awesome, merging the discussion into the RFC epic. :rocket:
